haiku-low.q4: Users where hash(user_id) mod 100 is below 10, about 10% of users, fixed so a given user is always in or always out.
haiku-low.q5: It must be the current shadow alias, have a report under 24 hours old showing at least 7 days, under 0.5% errors, p99 under 80 ms, and the ML lead runs promote.
haiku-low.q6: Not decided. Product has not chosen whether a live A/B test comes between shadow and the switch, and this plan does not choose.

haiku-low.q8: After sending the response, the API enqueues features and items fire-and-forget; shadow workers run the shadow version separately, so the user's response never waits on it.

sonnet.q1: The fallback response: same shape, 20 popular item IDs with "fallback": true.
sonnet.q2: Requests keep using the existing rows already in the online store. Rows older than 6 hours count as missing, so after that the user has no fresh features and gets the fallback.
sonnet.q3: No. The response never waits on or uses shadow output, so nothing that goes wrong in shadow can slow or break the user's response.
sonnet.q4: Users where hash(user_id) mod 100 is below 10 (about 10% of users). A given user is always in or always out.
sonnet.q5: It must be the current shadow alias, with a report from the last 24 hours showing at least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5% and p99 inference latency under 80 ms. The ML lead must run the promote command (which records who and when), and the version must have passed the load-time feature check on instances. Whether a live A/B test is also required is undecided.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. Product has not decided; the plan does not choose, and the steps work either way.
sonnet.q7: Each instance polls the registry every 30 seconds. If the active alias points to a new version, it loads it in the background, runs the feature check, and if that passes swaps to the new model in one step. Requests already running finish on the old model. No redeploy is needed.
sonnet.q8: After the response is sent, the API puts a message on the shadow queue containing the user ID, features, active version number and its items, so the worker uses the features in the message. Shadow does not add latency because it runs after the response is sent, the enqueue is fire-and-forget, and the work happens in separate workers.
sonnet.q9: If the enqueue fails or the queue is full, the message is dropped. The response is unaffected. Worker errors are logged and not retried.
sonnet.q10: In the prediction log, one row per shadow run (time, user, shadow version, shadow items, active version, active items, latency, errored). A daily job reads it and writes a dated report per shadow version with days in shadow, error rate, p99 inference latency, and overlap between shadow items and the active items stored in the same row. Where the log is stored is not decided.
sonnet.q11: The feature check at load time compares the feature names the model needs, from the registry, against the feature list from the last materialization run. If it fails, the instance or shadow worker does not run that version, keeps its current model, and alerts.
sonnet.q12: A person moves the active alias back to previous. Instances poll the registry every 30 seconds, load the target in the background, run the feature check and swap. The 30 second poll plus load time keeps it within 1 minute, and no redeploy is needed.
